thread:
kai-docs: FYI I opened a docs PR to clarify SOC2-safe language around audit exports, show redaction vs pseudonymization tradeoffs, and add migration/snippet examples for Go and Ruby SDKs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/6450

ana-security: Thanks. Two quick things up front: (1) avoid first-person promises like 'we'll keep' or 'we keep', (2) be explicit about access controls and audit trails for exported data.

kai-docs: Current draft sentence: 'Audit logs are retained for 90 days by default; exports created for compliance may be retained longer under legal hold.' Thoughts?

ana-security: Wording I'd prefer: 'Customer audit logs are retained for 90 days by default. As required by law or contractual obligations, retention for specific exports may be extended; exported datasets are access-controlled and logged.' That removes ambiguous language.

harry-eng: I added two tiny SDK examples for v1->v2 migration: a Go snippet showing a sampled query and a Ruby example showing a full export request. Drop them in if helpful.

harry-eng: Go sampling example:
```go
package main
import (
  "fmt"
  "github.com/redwood/inference-go"
)
func main() {
  c := inference.NewAuditClient("$REDWOOD_KEY")
  resp, _ := c.QueryEvents(map[string]interface{}{"sample":0.02, "start":"2025-06-01", "end":"2025-06-30"})
  fmt.Println(resp.Total)
}
```

harry-eng: Ruby full export example:
```ruby
require 'redwood'
client = Redwood::AuditClient.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])
# request complete export manifest for a date range
resp = client.create_export({ start: '2025-06-01', end: '2025-06-30', mode: 'full' })
puts resp['manifest_id']
```

kai-docs: Nice. Legal, any preferred phrasing about pseudonymized identifiers in examples? I have a short section contrasting redaction vs pseudonymization and an illustrative JSON.

tom-legal: Use the phrase 'example identifiers are pseudonymized' and include legal contact for holds: legal@redwood.com. Also add privacy contact: privacy@redwood.com for DPO-style questions. For retention wording, include 'as required by law or contractual obligations' as ana suggested.

kai-docs: Added legal+privacy contacts. For the redaction vs pseudonymization snippet I kept it short and non-prescriptive. Example pseudonymized event:
```json
{
  "user_id": "sha256:7d4b2a...",
  "action": "model.generate",
  "timestamp": "2025-06-15T14:22:00Z"
}
```

ana-security: Add a tiny callout about sampling bias: sampled queries are useful for rapid operational triage but can under-represent rare anomalies; recommend requesting a full export prior to formal compliance investigations. Also include a note that exported manifests include an HMAC for integrity checks.

kai-docs: Added sampling-bias callout and the HMAC note. I also included a link to the internal TTL override form and the export manifest schema (internal links).

harry-eng: One more tech nit: suggest calling out that 'export' means a complete dump compatible with our manifest schema v1.2 and that sampling is a statistical subset. Keeps expectations clear for customers.

kai-docs: Good point — added brief clarification and a tiny manifest example (fields only).

tom-legal: LGTM pending one small wording tweak: replace 'may be retained longer' with 'may be retained longer as required by law or contractual obligations' — pushable as an inline suggestion.

kai-docs: Pushed the tweak and requested final ack from security + legal. Will wait to merge until both have LGTM and CI linkcheck passes. @doc-bot can you add 'security-reviewed' label on merge?

doc-bot: PR updated: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/6450/files  reviewers requested: @ana-security @tom-legal @harry-eng

ci-bot: Linkcheck queued. Please ensure internal links are accessible from the docs pipeline.

kai-docs: Thanks everyone. Merge target: Thursday after linkcheck + two signoffs.
